note: Finding: `Extraction.Bound.volume` bounds the lattice values on compact K ⊆ Conf_n, the private `Extraction.extendsBound` passes this to the volume tables at single generic points, and `Extraction.volume_oscillates` derives equicontinuity from `Extraction.TransferLip`. No declaration differentiates the volume kernels f_{p,v} or bounds their derivatives.

verdicts.summary: [L] states no counterpart of what [M] prints. [M] prints `\sup_{p\ge p_0}\sup_{x\in K'}|\partial_{\boldsymbol l}f_{p,v}(x)| \le B(v,\boldsymbol l,r)`.
evidence: [M] prints sup_{p>=p0} sup_{x in K'} |partial_l f_{p,v}(x)| <= B(v,l,r) for every derivative list l. In [L], Bound.volume bounds only values, 'norm (lifted C N p v b) <= D', and extendsBound concludes only 'eventually norm ((P (f.per i)).read x v) <= D' at a point. Equicontinuity (volume_oscillates) comes from TransferLip, not from a derivative bound. Order.Meshes gives the volume kernels P p only 'ContinuousOn ... (Cyclic C.S p n)', so [L] never differentiates them. Smoothness of the limit S comes later, from distributional derivatives (Dash/Quot, Dash.awake, RawLimits.ready). The l != 0 bound therefore has no counterpart in [L]. This is not a typo: the proof's argument is built on it ('One more derivative bounds variation').

[M] prints sup_{p>=p0} sup_{x in K'} |d_l f_{p,v}(x)| <= B(v,l,r) for every derivative list l. [L]'s Bound has only value fields (cyclic, volume: ||lifted ...|| <= D); extendsBound gives a pointwise value bound and volume_oscillates gives uniform equicontinuity of values from the TransferLip hypothesis, and first_surface extracts only continuous limits (RawLimits.regular is ContinuousOn). No derivative bound on lattice kernels or on f_{p,v} exists in YM/Extraction; smoothness of the limit (Table.Smooth) is taken as a hypothesis in later lemmas, not derived. So the derivative bound for l != 0 has no counterpart; not a typo.
